equation_request.abstract: We show that any unitary operator on the $d_{A}\times d_{B}$ system ($d_{A}\geq 2$) can be decomposed into the product of at most $4d_{A}-5$ controlled unitary operators. The number can be reduced to $2d_{A}-1$ when $d_{A}$ is a power of two. We also prove that three controlled unitaries can implement a bipartite complex permutation operator, and discuss the connection to an analogous result on classical reversible circuits. We further show that any $n$-partite unitary on the space $\mathbb{C}^{d_{1}}\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathbb{C}^{d_{n}}$ is the product of at most $[2\prod^{n-1}_{j=1}(2d_{j}-2)-1]$ controlled unitary gates, each of which is controlled from $n-1$ systems. We also decompose any bipartite unitary into the product of a simple type of bipartite gates and some local unitaries. We derive dimension-independent upper bounds for the CNOT-gate cost or entanglement cost of bipartite permutation unitaries (with the help of ancillas of fixed size) as functions of the Schmidt rank of the unitary. It is shown that such costs under a simple protocol are related to the log-rank conjecture in communication complexity theory via the link of nonnegative rank.

specification.problem: Implement a bipartite permutation unitary P on C^{dA} x C^{dB} (|a,b> -> |pi(a,b)>) using only standard gates, with few CNOTs across the A|B cut, via the operator-Schmidt decomposition and a nonnegative-rank-style protocol. Verify on tiny instances (e.g. dA=dB=2) by reading the unitary or statevector.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One tiny instance: dA=dB=2 (1 qubit each), P = CNOT with A as control, operator-Schmidt rank r=2. Build it as a sum of 2 product terms using one ebit/CNOT-equivalent across the cut, in a gate-teleportation style (non-local CNOT through a Bell pair), and check unitary equality with P and ancillas returning to |0>. The general r_+ protocol, the 4dA-5 and 2dA-1 controlled-unitary bounds, the n-partite bound, and the log-rank link are outside scope.

symbols.domain: 0/1 matrix of size dA^2 x dB^2

equations.label: Operator-Schmidt decomposition
equations.description: Any bipartite operator is a sum of r product operators; r is the Schmidt rank of U.
equations.abstract_quote: as functions of the Schmidt rank of the unitary
equations.justification: The abstract uses the Schmidt rank of the unitary as the cost parameter, which presupposes this decomposition.

equations.label: Permutation as 0/1 matrix and communication matrix
equations.description: P is a real 0/1 matrix; its operator-Schmidt rank equals the rank of the reshaped (communication) matrix M.
equations.abstract_quote: related to the log-rank conjecture in communication complexity theory via the link of nonnegative rank
equations.justification: The link to log-rank and nonnegative rank implies this reshaping. The rank equality is standard linear algebra.
assumptions: Reshaping is by row index (a,a') and column index (b,b')

equations.label: Nonnegative factorization
equations.latex: M=\sum_{k=1}^{r_+}u_k v_k^{T},\quad u_k\ge0,\ v_k\ge0,\quad r\le r_+
equations.description: Nonnegative rank gives the number of rounds or terms in the protocol.
equations.abstract_quote: related to the log-rank conjecture in communication complexity theory via the link of nonnegative rank
equations.justification: The abstract links the cost to nonnegative rank. The explicit form is the standard definition.
assumptions: Cost is proportional to r_+ in a simple protocol, as the sketch says; the abstract does not give the exact form

equations.label: Toy instance: CNOT as two product terms
equations.description: The chosen instance has rank 2 and uses one ebit via non-local CNOT.
equations.justification: Smallest nontrivial permutation across the cut, chosen as the scoped instance.

equations.label: Success criterion
equations.description: The circuit W acts as P on the data registers and returns the ancillas to |0>.
equations.justification: Check required by the runner: compare the unitary or statevector against P.

registers.name: E
registers.role: Bell-pair ancillas, one on each side of the cut, returned to |0>

specification.initial_state: |a>_A|b>_B|00>_E; for the unitary check, prepare the Bell pair inside the circuit and uncompute it at the end

steps.description: Prepare a Bell pair on E (H on e0, CNOT e0->e1). This CNOT is local to ancilla preparation, but e1 is placed on Bob's side, so it counts as the one cut-crossing resource.

Non-local CNOT through the Bell pair: Alice does CNOT A->e0 and measures-free coherent correction. In a unitary-only version, implement the CNOT directly across the cut with one CNOT as a reference and compare it against the teleportation-style version.
Uncompute the flag and Bell pair by the reverse round so the ancillas return to |0>.
Read the full unitary (no measurements), restrict to ancilla=|0>, and compare to P up to global phase. Also check basis inputs |a,b>.

specification.classical_postprocessing: Classical: compute M from pi, its rank r (numpy), and optionally a nonnegative factorization to estimate r_+. Compare the circuit's unitary block to P.
assumptions: Cost is the CNOT count across the A|B cut, with local gates free
Ancillas have fixed size and return to |0>
Tiny instance dA=dB=2 chosen as scope
P is real 0/1 so nonnegative factorization applies
No measurements are used because the unitary or statevector is checked
missing_information: The exact protocol construction is not in the abstract; the coherent, measurement-free uncompute of the teleportation-style gate is unspecified
The precise relation between CNOT cost and r_+ (the abstract states only the link)
The controlled-unitary decomposition counts are not used here
